summary: Chittenden County, VT: a fire lookout was engaged for summer 1921 alongside the Taft Lodge custodian post; no tower, build date or removal found; FFLOS lists type unknown, abandoned.

facts.status_note: FFLOS lists the site as Abandoned with an unknown structure type; no source read describes a tower on the summit or its removal

access.note: Mount Mansfield is in Mount Mansfield State Forest with the Long Trail on the main ridge and a toll road to The Nose (Wikipedia). The lookout site itself is not described.

visit.trail_note: Long Trail along the main ridge; steep toll road from Stowe to The Nose (Wikipedia). No source describes lookout remains on the summit.

events.note: D. D. Holmes of Morristown engaged for the coming summer as fire lookout, per the Burlington Free Press (April 26, 1921), as quoted by Forest Lookouts

corrections.why: FFLOS lists the Mount Mansfield site type as Unknown. No source read describes a tower on the summit.
FFLOS lists the site as Abandoned, not gone. No source read says a structure was removed or destroyed, so 'gone' is not supported.

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The only lookout evidence is the April 1921 Burlington Free Press engagement, quoted by Forest Lookouts; no build date, structure, staffing history or fate was found. Taft Lodge (1920) is a Green Mountain Club shelter that the same man kept, not a lookout; the story keeps them apart. The FFLOS entry sits in its 'Lookout Sites / Other Structures' list, which matches an unknown type. Corrections proposed for kind (tower to unknown) and status (gone to unknown); please check against any state inventory before applying. Budget: 2 WebSearch calls; page reads: Forest Lookouts, FFLOS index, GMC 100 years, GMC caretakers page (no lookout match), Wikipedia, Vermont Daily Chronicle (no Mansfield lookout mention). Possible follow-up: Vermont state forestry annual reports for 1921-1925, and the Taft Lodge caretaker list, which may name later lookouts. No photos found.
